column3: Settings → Models: Test (credential.test) on each provider row, a health dot from models.catalog providers[].health with the error in a lazily loaded UI SDK Tooltip, every key save sends credential.set {test: true}, a Fallback models list (owner.fallbacks, saved as one owner.fallbacks.set, cap 8) in its own lazy chunk, and xin.fallback entries as a centred timeline note in place; the composer ModelPicker now anchors its popup to its trigger
column4: Test keeps focus while busy, so it is aria-disabled and ignores presses rather than disabled (a disabled button drops focus); the same idle/busy props serve Save and Discard on the fallback list. The list is a draft with one Save because a keyboard or drag reorder would otherwise send an op per step. saveCredential always tests, onboarding included, because a key that cannot answer is useless there too. The fallback note sits in the turn's segment order, not ahead of it the way xin.error is, so it reads where the switch happened. ModelPicker had no anchor: UI SDK Combobox then positions against its input, which lives inside the popup, so in Settings the popup chased itself across the screen (the composer hid it at the top edge); the combobox docs say to anchor an input-in-popup combobox to its button
